findings.statement: CA9 is strongly up in tumors at RNA (log2FC 6.312, padj 1.72e-49), protein (log2FC 2.269, padj 9.9e-43) and phospho (log2FC 1.91); RNA-protein Spearman rho 0.797. Membrane enzyme with girentuximab (Phase 3) as an antibody; a classic HIF-driven ccRCC marker.
COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is the top up-regulated protein (log2FC 3.768, padj 5.99e-48) with RNA log2FC 6.752; RNA-protein rho 0.634. A hypoxia-linked tumor marker, not a surface target.
NNMT is up at protein (log2FC 2.709, padj 1.23e-43) and RNA (log2FC 4.67, padj 2.04e-40), concordant across layers; a metabolic enzyme candidate target and tissue biomarker.
PLIN2 is up at protein (log2FC 2.667) and RNA (log2FC 2.62), consistent with the lipid-droplet-rich clear-cell phenotype; 16.4% of tumors show copy loss.
PFKP is up at protein (log2FC 2.863, padj 7.05e-45) and RNA (log2FC 2.72), a glycolytic enzyme reflecting the Warburg shift under VHL loss.
MET is up at RNA (log2FC 1.342) and protein (log2FC 1.101) with 25.5% copy gain; druggable (savolitinib Phase 3, telisotuzumab vedotin Phase 3).
EGFR is up at RNA (log2FC 1.461) and protein (log2FC 1.062) with 25.5% copy gain; has approved/late-stage agents (afatinib Phase 4, cetuximab sarotalocan approved).
CD74 is up at RNA (log2FC 1.775) and protein (log2FC 0.935) with 56.4% copy gain; milatuzumab (Phase 1/2) targets it. Likely partly immune-infiltrate signal.
CXCR4 is up at RNA (log2FC 2.859) and protein (log2FC 1.157); approved antagonists exist (plerixafor, mavorixafor). Possibly reflects immune infiltration.
EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) protein is up (log2FC 1.162) while RNA rises only modestly (0.306), indicating post-transcriptional stabilization under VHL loss; belzutifan is approved.
VHL lies on 3p with loss frequency 0.791 (gain 0.027) across 110 tumors, explaining HIF pathway activation.
PBRM1 on 3p shows loss frequency 0.8 (gain 0.027), consistent with 3p loss as the founding event.
ALDOB is strongly down at RNA (log2FC -7.028) reflecting loss of proximal tubule identity; a negative tissue marker, not a target.
ACY1 is down at RNA (log2FC -3.529) and protein (-2.305) with 80.9% copy loss, consistent with 3p-linked loss of tubule metabolism.
CHL1 protein is among the most down-regulated (log2FC -3.432, padj 2.06e-32) with RNA log2FC -3.117 and 77.3% copy loss.

caveats: Convergence score mixes omics with Open Targets, so immune genes (CD74, CXCR4, PTPRC) may reflect infiltrate rather than tumor cell expression.
Bulk tissue; paired n varies by layer (75 RNA, 84 protein).
Copy-number data lacks evidence ids for genes with frequency under 0.3.
Convergence score is not validated causally; targets need functional validation.
Phospho and drug evidence were not examined beyond CA9 and ranking output.

findings.statement: CA9 is the best-supported gene across omics, Open Targets (girentuximab, Phase 3) and literature. PMID:42473996 reports CA9 preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumor cells with low expression in normal kidney, CA9-targeted PET as proof-of-concept for noninvasive ccRCC discrimination 'warranting prospective validation', and high CA9-PET uptake associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function, reduced B-cell infiltration and enhanced angiogenic activity; CA9-high PDX models showed greater growth inhibition under axitinib. CAIX mRNA was also increased in HIV-associated kidney cancer (PMID:35795483). Evidence is proof-of-concept, not prospectively validated.

NDUFA4L2 (COXFA4L2) is upregulated in >90% of ccRCC (PMID:36722045), induced by HIF-1alpha/hypoxic signaling (PMID:42331208, 36722045), predicts poor survival and supports proliferation in cell lines (PMID:34970493), increases glycolysis, and enhances lipid deposition and Ca9 expression in the TRACK model. PMID:42331208 states it suppresses mitochondria-associated ferroptosis with LDHB and that targeting the NDUFA4L2/LDHB axis is a promising strategy, particularly with radiotherapy. It also marks low- and high-grade ccRCC in tissue-derived EVs (PMID:41656939). Largely preclinical; no ccRCC clinical validation in the corpus.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the only top-ranked gene with an approved ccRCC-relevant drug (belzutifan). The corpus states VHL inactivation leads to HIF-2alpha accumulation and that belzutifan has been FDA-approved for ccRCC (PMID:42422841); a review notes HIF-2alpha inhibitors as later-line options after ICI exposure (PMID:41941086). EPAS1 has zero extracted literature relations, so support comes from review sentences.

CD74 ranks 2nd by convergence (omics, CNV gain 56%, Open Targets) but has one ccRCC paper in the corpus (PMID:39080216, 'Potential protumor function of CD74'): IHC shows expression in cancer cells and macrophages, with function suggested to differ between the two and 'further studies are necessary'. Evidence is a single, descriptive study; part of the omics signal may reflect macrophage infiltration.

CXCR4 has strong omics (log2FC 2.86) and drugs (plerixafor approved for other indications), but one literature relation: a database-integration study (PMID:34266404) found C3 and CXCR4 overexpressed in ccRCC and associated with prognosis. This is a bioinformatic finding without experimental or clinical validation.

ENO2 is proposed as a diagnostic and independent prognostic biomarker in ccRCC (PMID:37760940), drives Warburg-type glycolysis, and its knockdown inhibits glycolysis and promotes ferroptosis (PMID:39091581). High ENO2 is associated with lower predicted sensitivity to axitinib, sunitinib, pazopanib and temsirolimus (PMID:36419844), and AXL and ENO2 are linked to lenvatinib/cabozantinib resistance (PMID:42869109). Another survival analysis also lists ENO2 (PMID:36313709). All findings are bioinformatic or cell-line based. NSE was a risk factor for intraocular metastasis in RCC (PMID:34467977).

The literature on MT1G is contradictory. PMID:36204178 reports MT1G downregulated in ccRCC and 'may be a negative regulator of ferroptosis ... and a biomarker of poor prognosis'. PMID:38906969 reports low MT1G in tumor tissue but high MT1G correlating with advanced stage and poorer prognosis; elevated MT1G promoted growth and metastasis, and MT1G inhibits CPT1B via H3K14 trimethylation to increase lipid droplets. PMID:40247376 shows SAP30 inhibits MT1G transcription, impairing zinc delivery to p53. The direction (tumor suppressor versus oncogenic) is not settled.

ALDOB is strongly downregulated in ccRCC (log2FC -7). PMID:40852386 confirms by IHC that it is diminished versus adjacent normal tissue, links it to infiltrating Treg, Th17 and neutrophils, and calls it 'a prognostic biomarker and a potential immunotherapy target'. PMID:38655323 reports it as an independent prognostic predictor in KIRC, and a pan-cancer study (PMID:37083815) found low expression across cancers. Evidence is retrospective and bioinformatic with limited IHC; the pan-cancer pattern limits specificity.

PFKP is upregulated in ccRCC (PMID:34321910, PMID:36901940, among the most consistently upregulated genes with PLIN2, VEGFA, CCND1) and listed as a glycolysis-related biomarker with strong diagnostic and prognostic potential (PMID:40341002). Contradiction: PMID:34321910 also reports that low PFKP expression correlates with poor 5- and 10-year OS despite upregulation in tumors. Bioinformatic signatures only.

PLIN2 is upregulated in ccRCC (PMID:36901940), related to prognosis in KIRC by GEPIA Kaplan-Meier analysis (PMID:35314744), and PLIN2 diagnostic potential was validated by IHC on 128 tissue-microarray samples for renal neoplasms (PMID:34482820). Support is for diagnostic and lipid-droplet biology; no therapeutic evidence in the corpus.

ABAT is downregulated in KIRC and KIRP and predicts poor prognosis in KIRC in a pan-cancer analysis (PMID:41158242). PMID:41813748 shows overexpression suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in vivo via cGAS-STING and PRMT5-enhanced interferon signaling. A separate study links ABAT and GABAergic shifts to sunitinib resistance (PMID:39100925). Note that low expression is reported with poor prognosis while tumor-suppressive function is shown, which is internally consistent, but the clinical link to sunitinib resistance is title-level only. Vigabatrin is a Phase 4 ABAT inhibitor, which would act in the opposite direction to a suppressor role.

CHL1 is lost in ccRCC (CNV loss 77%, protein log2FC -3.4). PMID:35262525 reports that ccRCC patients with low CHL1 had poorer overall survival (Kaplan-Meier P<0.001) and that low CHL1 'might predict poor OS'. This is a single retrospective expression study with no mechanistic or therapeutic evidence.

ACY1 is downregulated in ccRCC tissues alongside MAGI2-AS3, whose low expression is associated with poor survival (PMID:34002044). The ACY1 oncogene/radiotherapy-target statements (PMID:36428796) concern colorectal cancer, not ccRCC. ACY1 has no direct ccRCC prognostic or therapeutic evidence, and the CRC data suggest the opposite functional direction.

caveats: Many top-ranked genes (EGFR, FAS, PIGR, GRAMD4, ERBB2, TNFRSF10B, ATP1A1, PTPRC, PDGFRA, FHIT, SCARB1, AGMAT, GPC3, IKZF1, DDC, KDR, TNFAIP3, CARD11, NDRG1, PBX1, RUNX1, MECOM, PTPN13) have 0 extracted literature relations; their rank rests on omics, shared somatic-mutation scores (identical 0.4559 values suggest a generic Open Targets feature) and tractability, not ccRCC literature. EGFR and KDR searches returned no ccRCC-specific sentences.

Literature scores of 1.0 for ACY1, MT1G, ALDOB, PLIN2, COXFA4L2, ENO2, SAP30, ABAT and PFKP reflect relation counts in this corpus, not clinical validity; most evidence is TCGA/GEO bioinformatics, cell lines or single-center IHC.

Contradictions: MT1G (low in tumor yet high expression linked to poor prognosis/oncogenic), PFKP (up in tumor yet low expression linked to poor OS), ACY1 (downregulated in ccRCC but oncogene in CRC), ABAT (suppressor versus vigabatrin inhibitor drug).
Clinically validated items are limited to belzutifan/HIF-2alpha and VEGFR-TKI/ICI standards of care (review sentences); CA9 PET is proof-of-concept needing prospective validation.
The corpus (~320 abstracts) is small; absence of sentences does not mean absence of evidence in the wider literature. Chunk searches were not exhaustive for each gene.

Drugs: GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_3, IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_2, SULTHIAME PHASE_4, ETHOXZOLAMIDE WITHDRAWAL. UniProt Q16790: cell membrane / microvillus membrane, which suits antibody/radioligand imaging and a tissue or serum biomarker. Untested as an approved ccRCC drug target, but the best-supported membrane biomarker.

Established ccRCC target (HIF-2alpha). Convergence rank 38 (score 3.2903). Open Targets association 0.4871 (genetic 0.5677, somatic 0.4559, literature 0.4802). Drug: BELZUTIFAN APPROVAL. UniProt Q99814: nuclear transcription factor, so not an antibody or biomarker target. RNA log2FC only 0.306 (protein 1.162), so its effect is post-transcriptional (VHL loss stabilises the protein).

Drugs returned include RIVOCERANIB MESYLATE APPROVAL, VATALANIB PHASE_3, LINIFANIB PHASE_3, XL-820 PHASE_2. Other VEGFR-targeted agents (sunitinib, pazopanib, axitinib, etc.) appear in the FLT4 drug list. UniProt P35968: cell-membrane receptor tyrosine kinase for VEGFA/C/D.

Established VEGFR family member (VEGFR3). Open Targets ccRCC association 0.4549 (top-25 disease target). Tractable modalities AB, PR, SM. Drugs include TIVOZANIB APPROVAL, AXITINIB APPROVAL, PAZOPANIB HYDROCHLORIDE APPROVAL, LENVATINIB MESYLATE APPROVAL, SORAFENIB TOSYLATE APPROVAL, SUNITINIB MALATE PHASE_4, CABOZANTINIB not listed. These are multikinase agents, so the FLT4 label reflects polypharmacology and not FLT4-selective validation.

Established ccRCC target. Open Targets association 0.525 (6th among ccRCC targets, after VHL, PBRM1, KDM5C, BAP1 and SETD2). Tractability AB, PR, SM (SM: Approved Drug). Drugs include RIDAFOROLIMUS APPROVAL, GEDATOLISIB PHASE_3, DACTOLISIB PHASE_3, SAPANISERTIB PHASE_2, VISTUSERTIB PHASE_2. Reactome: mTORC1-mediated signalling, PIP3 activates AKT signaling. The everolimus/temsirolimus rapalogs are not in the returned list, so check ChEMBL names separately.

Drugs: SAVOLITINIB PHASE_3, TELISOTUZUMAB VEDOTIN PHASE_3, FORETINIB PHASE_2, SGX-523 PHASE_1. UniProt P08581: membrane and secreted forms. A tractable, clinically tested (papillary RCC) candidate with consistent RNA and protein up-regulation in this ccRCC cohort.

RNA log2FC 1.775, protein log2FC 0.935, CNV gain 56.4% (highest gain frequency among the top candidates). Drugs: MILATUZUMAB PHASE_1_2 (anti-CD74 antibody); REPOTRECTINIB APPROVAL is probably an off-target annotation. UniProt P04233: cell membrane and secreted. Likely reflects immune-infiltrate signal in addition to tumour-cell expression.

Drugs: PLERIXAFOR APPROVAL, MAVORIXAFOR APPROVAL, MOTIXAFORTIDE APPROVAL, BURIXAFOR PHASE_2, MSX-122 PHASE_1. UniProt P61073: cell-membrane GPCR. Approved drugs exist for other indications, so repurposing is plausible but untested in ccRCC.

Convergence rank 1 (score 3.87, 5 streams). Open Targets association 0.3049 (somatic 0.4559, literature 0.3308). RNA log2FC 1.461, protein log2FC 1.062, CNV gain 25.5%. Drugs: AFATINIB PHASE_4, CETUXIMAB SAROTALOCAN APPROVAL, RUSERONTINIB PHASE_3, TESEVATINIB PHASE_3. Tractable and consistently up-regulated, but not an established ccRCC drug target (approvals are for other cancers).

Convergence rank 5 (score 3.7768). Open Targets association 0.4532 (genetic 0.7338; 16th among ccRCC targets). Strongly down-regulated in tumour (RNA log2FC -3.824, protein -1.235). No drugs. UniProt P01833: cell membrane and secreted, so it is a plausible loss-of-expression tissue or fluid biomarker. Association-only gene.

Convergence rank 11 (score 3.5677). Open Targets association 0.4265 (genetic 0.5552; top-25 target). RNA log2FC 1.01, protein 1.047. Drugs: DULANERMIN PHASE_2, DROZITUMAB PHASE_2, TIGATUZUMAB PHASE_2, LBY-135 PHASE_1, APOMAB PHASE_1 (TRAIL-R2 agonists, untested in ccRCC). Tractable but untested.

Convergence rank 28 (score 3.3318, 4 streams). Open Targets association only 0.0272 (literature 0.141), but literature relations in the graph (3) and strong concordant up-regulation (RNA log2FC 2.62, protein 2.667). No drugs. UniProt Q99541: lipid droplet protein, consistent with the lipid-laden clear-cell phenotype. Candidate tissue biomarker, not a drug target.

Top Open Targets ccRCC association (0.6466, rank 1). PBRM1 is next (0.6348). VHL loss drives HIF-2alpha (EPAS1) stabilisation, which underlies the VEGF, CA9 and PLIN2 programmes above. VHL itself is not directly druggable; the therapeutic route is through EPAS1 (belzutifan).

caveats: Convergence scores in the top ranks (about 3.3 to 3.9) are dominated by omics and a shared somatic-mutation score of 0.4559, which is identical across many genes. This is probably a generic OT somatic score, not ccRCC-specific driver evidence.
Open Targets drug lists include off-target or unrelated-indication annotations (for example REPOTRECTINIB for CD74, PERHEXILINE for MTOR), and the 'max stage' is not specific to ccRCC.
Established ccRCC agents (everolimus, temsirolimus, cabozantinib, nivolumab) were not checked individually; MTOR and FLT4 lists were truncated to the returned records.
STRING interactions were not queried because of time or budget; the pathway context relies on Reactome labels from the target profiles.
Published-literature support for PIGR, CD74 and CXCR4 in ccRCC was not independently verified.

findings.statement: CA9 is tumor-intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of tumor transcripts (54.7% of 10900 RCC cells express it; PT 2.6%), and tumor cells vs proximal tubule give log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189, 6 donors, PT mean log2CPM 0.0). Bulk RNA log2FC 6.312.

In situ, CA9-high spots (n=3585) are surrounded by RCC (observed 0.4962 vs expected 0.384, log2 enrichment 0.37, padj 0.00167) with composition-corrected RCC share 0.999; macrophage enrichment is marginal (log2 0.084).

Structural caveat: best CA9 site MGD score is only 0.546 (volume 126.8 A3, 1 accessible lysine, pocket pLDDT 90.3; mean pLDDT 76.56). Ligand-site recall 0.5 overall but 0.221 in top pockets. A modest site, not a prediction of a degrader; CA9 is better suited to antibody/imaging (girentuximab) than glue.

EGFR ranks first in convergence (score 3.87, 5 streams; RNA log2FC 1.461, protein 1.062). RCC cells hold 0.948 of tumor transcripts but only 29.7% of RCC cells express it, so the signal is tumor-intrinsic but sparse.

Tumor cells vs proximal tubule: log2FC 4.748 (pvalue 0.00449, padj 0.0714, 6 donors), so not significant at padj<0.05; PT also expresses EGFR (15.4% of cells). High spots (n=3751) are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 0.263, padj 0.00167).

Top EGFR site scores 0.7304 (volume 189.9 A3, 6 accessible lysines, pocket pLDDT 85.9, mean pLDDT 75.94); it lies in the kinase region, so a glue site claim needs caution. Ligand-site recall 0.375 (0.11 in top pockets).

MET is tumor-intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.935 of tumor transcripts (35.2% expressing); endothelium contributes 0.03. Tumor vs PT log2FC 5.237 (pvalue 0.00407, padj 0.069, 6 donors), not significant at padj<0.05. Bulk RNA log2FC 1.342.
MET-high spots (n=3674) are enriched for RCC (log2 0.203, padj 0.00167) and NK neighbours (log2 0.17, padj 0.00167); composition-corrected RCC share 0.971.

MET best site score 0.6789 is driven by lysines (8) and degron loop, but its volume is only 27.6 A3 (geometry 0.0), a shallow pocket; ligand-site recall 0.439 (0.095 in top pockets). Weak glue pocket despite the score.

EPAS1 (HIF-2a) transcripts are mostly stromal in scRNA: Endothelial 0.365 share (81.3% expressing), Fibroblast 0.081, RCC only 0.051 (4.9% expressing). Tumor vs PT log2FC 0.589 (padj 0.665), no tumor-cell-specific RNA gain; bulk signal is largely microenvironment RNA, and HIF-2a activity is post-transcriptional.

EPAS1-high spots (n=3757) are enriched for fibroblast (log2 0.327) and endothelial (log2 0.267) neighbours, padj 0.00167. Best MGD site 0.6709 has low confidence: mean pLDDT 58.56, only 3 accessible lysines, so a glue site is poorly supported.

KDR is an endothelial (microenvironment) target, not a tumor-cell target: endothelium holds 0.951 of tumor transcripts (40.5% of endothelial cells), and in situ corrected endothelial share is 0.99 with RCC 0.002. High spots are enriched for endothelial neighbours (log2 0.286, padj 0.00167).

KDR holds the second best MGD site overall (0.841; volume 361.1 A3, 7 accessible lysines, pocket pLDDT 83.1, mean pLDDT 71.12) in the kinase region; ligand-site recall 0.4 (0.2 in top pockets). Target cell is endothelium (anti-angiogenic logic).

CD74 is immune/myeloid: macrophages hold 0.436 of tumor transcripts, CD8 T 0.345, cDC 0.114 (cDC 100% expressing; macrophage 99.5%). Convergence rank 2 (score 3.8535, RNA log2FC 1.775) therefore reflects infiltrate, not tumor cells. In situ RCC share is 0.174 vs macrophage 0.596; high spots neighbour T cells (log2 0.407) and macrophages (log2 0.235).

CXCR4 is lymphocyte-borne: CD8 T hold 0.563 of tumor transcripts (72.9% expressing), CD4 T 0.176 (87.8%). Bulk RNA log2FC 2.859 reflects T/B cell infiltration. High spots neighbour B cells (log2 0.292) and T cells.
CXCR4 best MGD score 0.7066 but pocket volume 1149.5 A3 (near large-void territory), only 1 accessible lysine, mean pLDDT 82.25 (GPCR): a weak glue candidate.

ERBB2 is down in tumor (RNA log2FC -1.38, protein -0.692) despite a high MGD site (0.7821, volume 415.6 A3, 6 lysines, pLDDT 74); main expresser RCC with share 0.453, so it is a weaker tumor target than EGFR/MET.

PTPRC (CD45) is a pan-leukocyte marker: CD8 T hold 0.574 of tumor transcripts; it has the top MGD score (0.8462; volume 1142.4 A3, 5 lysines, pLDDT 76.06) but its up-regulation (RNA log2FC 2.071) reports immune infiltration, not tumor cells.

caveats: scRNA has 12 donors; tumor-vs-PT comparison uses 6 donors and PT has only 39 cells from 1 donor in tumor tissue; EGFR and MET are not significant at padj<0.05.
Endothelium is 1202 cells from 5 donors; CA9 and EGFR sparsity (30-55% expressing) reflects dropout.
Spatial enrichments are small in effect size (log2 0.04-0.4) although BH-significant; Visium spots mix cell types.

MGD scores rank sites only; none implies an existing or effective glue. Large voids (>1500 A3) are excluded as glue pockets. AlphaFold models are apo, and ligand-site recall is 0.375-0.5 for genes checked.
CXCR4 and PTPRC are immune targets; EPAS1 structure is low confidence (mean pLDDT 58.56).
CD74/CXCR4 structure_pockets were not run; their MGD values are from mgd_ranking.

summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest convergent evidence. It is strongly up-regulated in tumors at RNA and protein level, it is the most tumor-intrinsic candidate in single-cell and spatial data (clearly specific versus proximal tubule), it has the largest set of validated literature relations among druggable genes, and an antibody (girentuximab) has reached Phase 3. It is best positioned as a target_and_biomarker for antibody, radioligand and PET imaging approaches.

The VHL / HIF-2alpha axis is the mechanistic backbone: 3p loss (VHL, PBRM1) is near-universal, EPAS1 protein rises without a matching RNA increase, and belzutifan is approved. Established anti-angiogenic targets (KDR, FLT4) and MTOR are confirmed by Open Targets, but KDR and most EPAS1 RNA sit in endothelial and stromal cells, so these act on the microenvironment rather than on tumor-cell RNA levels.

The top of the numeric convergence ranking (EGFR, CD74, FAS, CXCR4, PIGR, MET) is driven largely by omics plus a shared Open Targets somatic score and tractability, with little ccRCC-specific literature in this corpus. Cell-type data split this group: EGFR and MET are tumor-intrinsic (though not significant versus proximal tubule), whereas CD74, CXCR4 and PTPRC are immune-infiltrate signals and should not be read as tumor-cell targets.

Biomarker-oriented candidates are dominated by the hypoxic and lipid-laden clear-cell phenotype (COXFA4L2/NDUFA4L2, PLIN2, PFKP, NNMT up; ALDOB, ACY1, CHL1, PIGR down as markers of lost tubule identity). Literature support for these is mostly bioinformatic or single-center, with outright contradictions for PFKP and MT1G.

omics.text: CA9 is strongly up in tumors at RNA (log2FC 6.312), protein (log2FC 2.269) and phospho levels, with RNA-protein Spearman rho 0.797.
COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is the top up-regulated protein (log2FC 3.768) with RNA log2FC 6.752, a hypoxia-linked marker rather than a surface target.
EPAS1 protein is up (log2FC 1.162) while RNA rises only modestly (0.306), consistent with post-transcriptional stabilization of HIF-2alpha after VHL loss.

VHL (loss frequency 0.791) and PBRM1 (0.8) on 3p are lost in most tumors, the founding event that activates the HIF program; tubule-identity genes such as ACY1 (80.9% copy loss) and CHL1 are strongly down.

literature.text: CA9 has the most direct ccRCC literature support: enrichment in ccRCC tumor cells with low normal-kidney expression and CA9-targeted PET as proof-of-concept for noninvasive discrimination, which still warrants prospective validation.
NDUFA4L2 (COXFA4L2) is reported as upregulated in most ccRCC, HIF-induced, linked to poor survival and to ferroptosis suppression; the evidence is largely preclinical.

Literature is contradictory for MT1G (low in tumor yet high expression linked to poor prognosis) and PFKP (up in tumor yet low expression linked to poor survival), and many top-ranked genes (EGFR, FAS, PIGR, KDR, ERBB2) have no extracted ccRCC relations in this corpus.

external.text: Open Targets confirms EPAS1 (belzutifan, approved), KDR and FLT4 (VEGFR-directed kinase inhibitors) and MTOR as established ccRCC targets; FLT4 drug labels reflect multikinase polypharmacology.
MET is tractable and clinically tested elsewhere (savolitinib and telisotuzumab vedotin at Phase 3), with membrane localization in UniProt.
VHL has the top Open Targets ccRCC association (0.6466) but is not directly druggable; the therapeutic route runs through EPAS1.

cells.text: CA9 is tumor-intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of tumor transcripts and the tumor-cell versus proximal-tubule comparison gives log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189).
EGFR (RCC share 0.948) and MET (RCC share 0.935) are expressed by tumor cells, but neither reaches padj<0.05 versus proximal tubule (EGFR padj 0.0714, MET padj 0.069).

Several bulk-omics candidates are not tumor-intrinsic: KDR is endothelial (share 0.951), EPAS1 RNA is mostly endothelial and fibroblast (RCC share 0.051), CD74 is macrophage/CD8 T-cell borne, and CXCR4 is lymphocyte-borne (CD8 T share 0.563).

spatial.text: CA9-high Visium spots are surrounded by RCC (log2 enrichment 0.37, padj 0.00167), consistent with tumor-cell expression in situ.

EGFR- and MET-high spots are enriched for RCC neighbours, whereas KDR-high spots neighbour endothelium, EPAS1-high spots neighbour fibroblasts and endothelium, and CD74-high spots neighbour T cells and macrophages; effect sizes are small.

structure.text: MGD scores rank predicted pockets, not degraders. The highest-ranked sites belong to PTPRC (0.8462) and KDR (0.841), both non-tumor-cell targets; ERBB2 (0.7821) and EGFR (0.7304) follow, with EGFR's site in the kinase region.
Several scores overstate site quality: MET's best site is only 27.6 A3, CXCR4's is 1149.5 A3 with one accessible lysine, and EPAS1's model has low confidence (mean pLDDT 58.56).
CA9's best site scores a modest 0.546, so CA9 is better suited to antibody or imaging approaches than to a molecular glue.

integration.text: Omics, literature, external knowledge and cell context converge most clearly on CA9: strong concordant up-regulation, tumor-intrinsic expression, literature support and a Phase 3 antibody.

The main disagreement is between numeric rank and cell context: CD74 and CXCR4 rank in the top four but are immune-borne, while EPAS1 ranks only 38th yet is the clinically validated target because its activity is post-transcriptional. I therefore promote EPAS1 and the VEGFR axis and demote immune genes in the target list.

limitations.text: Omics are bulk tumor-versus-normal tissue (paired n varies by layer), so immune and stromal genes can appear as tumor up-regulation.
The numeric convergence score is inflated for many genes by an identical Open Targets somatic score, which looks generic rather than ccRCC-specific.
The literature corpus is small (~320 abstracts); absence of relations does not mean absence of published evidence, and most relations are bioinformatic or single-center.
Single-cell tumor-versus-proximal-tubule comparisons use 6 donors with few proximal-tubule cells; EGFR and MET do not reach padj<0.05.
MGD scores rank predicted pockets on apo AlphaFold models; they are not evidence that any degrader exists or would work.
STRING interactions were not queried and established agents such as everolimus, cabozantinib and nivolumab were not checked individually.

targets.rationale: Strongest multi-layer convergence: RNA log2FC 6.312 and protein log2FC 2.269, tumor-intrinsic (log2FC 7.739 versus proximal tubule), validated literature relations including CA9-PET, and girentuximab at Phase 3. Ranked first despite numeric rank 10 because no other candidate is supported by every layer.
Clinically validated (belzutifan approved). Protein is up while RNA is flat, so bulk and single-cell RNA understate it; this is why it ranks only 38th numerically and is promoted here.
Established anti-angiogenic target with approved VEGFR inhibitors; it is endothelial (share 0.951), not tumor-intrinsic, so it acts on the tumor vasculature.

Concordant RNA and protein up-regulation with 25.5% copy gain, tumor-intrinsic expression (RCC share 0.935) and Phase 3 agents; weaker than CA9 because it is not significant versus proximal tubule and its best pocket is shallow.

Numeric rank 1 with RNA and protein up-regulation and approved agents in other cancers; tumor-intrinsic but sparse (29.7% of RCC cells) and not significant versus proximal tubule, with no ccRCC literature relations, so placed below MET.
Established ccRCC pathway target in Open Targets (association 0.525) with an approved small-molecule drug; included for clinical relevance although it is not in the omics top 25.
Top up-regulated protein (log2FC 3.768) with HIF-linked biology and poor-survival associations in the literature; a strong tissue biomarker, with therapeutic claims still preclinical.
Concordant up-regulation (RNA log2FC 2.62, protein 2.667) reflecting the lipid-laden clear-cell phenotype, with IHC diagnostic validation reported; no drugs.
Up at protein (log2FC 2.863) and RNA (log2FC 2.72) as part of the glycolytic shift; literature is contradictory on prognosis, so it is listed as a biomarker rather than a target.

Numeric rank 5, strongly down-regulated (RNA log2FC -3.824) with Open Targets genetic association 0.7338 and a membrane/secreted form; a loss-of-expression biomarker without literature support in this corpus.
Numeric rank 2, but single-cell data place its RNA mainly in macrophages (0.436) and CD8 T cells (0.345); demoted to a microenvironment biomarker rather than a tumor-cell target.

Numeric rank 4 with approved antagonists, but its up-regulation reflects lymphocyte infiltration (CD8 T share 0.563) and literature support is a single bioinformatic study; demoted to an immune biomarker.
